newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Flammarion seeks to buy monthly magazines.
newsitem.headline: France's Flammarion seeks to buy monthly magazines.

text.p: French book and magazine publisher Flammarion is looking this year "for buying opportunities in monthly general magazines and in books," chairman Charles-Henri Flammarion said on Wednesday.

Flammarion, announcing a sharp rise in the publisher's 1996 net attributable profit, told a news conference that his company planned to invest 25 million francs this year, up from 20 million in 1996, excluding acquisitions.

The publisher's net attributable profit rose to 51.9 million francs in 1996 from 32.4 million a year earlier, including a one-off capital gain from a disposal of 13.5 million francs, it said in a statement.
The net attributable profit -- excluding the capital gain and depreciation of goodwill from acquisitions -- rose 18 percent to 39.9 million francs.
Turnover was 1.11 billion francs compared with 1.01 billion in 1995.
The company had net cash of 91 million francs at the end of last year, up from 80.9 million at end-1995.
Last year it spent 17 million francs on buying arts magazine Beaux Arts and 16 million francs on taking a 48 percent stake in Pygmalion, a publisher of novels and history books.
Flammarion did not exclude his company taking a bigger stake in Pygmalion, but said its current stake would only be consolidated from 1997 in Flammarion's results.
French publishing could see a small slide in its overall turnover this year, he added. In 1996 the sector showed stable turnover at 14 billion francs.
He also said business in CD Roms was not growing as well as expected. Flammarion would remain cautious in this sector, the chairman said.
